item.title: Director Of Legislative And Government Affairs
item.description: Job Description The Director of Legislative and Government Affairs at Eccalon is responsible for leading the development and execution of policies and strategic objectives related to local, state, and federal government affairs on behalf of the company. In this role, the Director cultivates and maintains strong, productive relationships with government entities, regulatory authorities, legislative committees, and key policymakers. Serving as Eccalon's primary legislative advocate, the Director represents and safeguards the company's interests in the public policy arena while advising senior leadership on the establishment of corporate strategies, policies, and operational plans to ensure full alignment with evolving government laws, regulations, and industry standards. Responsibilities Develop and implement government affairs strategies to advance organizational goals Monitor legislative, regulatory, and political developments that impact the organization Engage with legislators, regulators, government agencies, and their staff to advocate for the organization's policy objectives Build and maintain relationships with elected officials, policymakers, regulatory agencies, and external stakeholders Lead the creation of policy positions, advocacy materials, and strategic recommendations for senior leadership Oversee the drafting of policy briefs, position statements, comment letters, and related materials Represent the organization at hearings, meetings, industry associations, and public forums Provide regular briefings to executive leadership on the political landscape, strategic opportunities, and potential threats Collaborate with internal teams to assess policy impacts and align advocacy efforts Track, analyze, and report on policy trends and emerging issues Ensure compliance with lobbying regulations, reporting requirements, and internal policies Manage PAC activities (if applicable), including compliance with FEC rules and all applicable laws, managing strategy, and overseeing reporting and record keeping. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in public policy, political science, government, public administration, or a related field Master's degree in public policy, law, business, or a related field is desired 10+ years of experience in government affairs, public policy, legislative work, or regulatory engagement Proven experience working with elected officials, policymakers, and industry coalitions

item.title: Government Affairs Operations Analyst
item.description: Your Impact The Government Affairs Operations Analyst provides integrated policy research, operational, logistical and administrative support to advance Lowe's public policy and government relations priorities. This role monitors and evaluates legislative, regulatory, and administrative developments; prepares clear, actionable analyses; and maintains accurate records and compliance documentation. This position also supports the efficient operation of the Washington, DC office and government affairs team through scheduling, budget tracking, invoice and expense processing, travel and event coordination, and executive support. The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, discreet, and able to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment with senior leaders and external stakeholders. What You Will Do Analyze government affairs activities, campaigns, and stakeholder engagement efforts and provide support for compliance analysis, administration, and applicable federal, state, and local reporting requirements. Gather intelligence and support preparation of legislative testimony, policy positions, executive briefings, and presentations related to pending or emerging legislative and regulatory matters. Develop project plans, timelines, run-of-show documents, and other planning materials to coordinate internal teams, external vendors, and business partners through program and event execution. Monitor, analyze, and report on legislative, regulatory, and public policy developments impacting Lowe’s; identify emerging trends and issues and support development of position papers, policy briefings, presentations, and other materials for business and government affairs leadership. Coordinate with vendors and service providers, including sourcing support, pricing discussions, deliverables, timelines, and contract-related activities in partnership with procurement, legal, and finance. Serve as a key point of contact for Washington, DC office operations and contribute to special projects and process improvements that strengthen the effectiveness of the government affairs team. Support the planning and execution of government affairs meetings, fly-ins, conferences, receptions, stakeholder engagements, and other events, including logistics, communications, briefing materials, registration, and onsite coordination. Track the government affairs budget and program-related expenses; process invoices, purchase orders, sponsorships, and vendor payments; and partner with finance to reconcile spending and support forecasting. Support government affairs leadership and senior executives with briefing materials, schedules, travel, meeting preparation, stakeholder information, and event logistics. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in political science, public policy, law, government, business administration, communications, or a related field or equivalent years of experience in lieu of education requirement, if applicable 3 years of experience in government affairs, legal research, public policy, regulatory affairs, corporate affairs, administrative operations, or a related field. Strong research, analytical, writing, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate complex legal or policy issues to non-legal audiences. Demonstrated organizational and project-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and sensitive matters accurately. Experience maintaining legislative, regulatory, stakeholder, compliance, budget, or project trackers with a high degree of accuracy. Ability to handle confidential information with discretion and professionalism. Preferred Skills/Education Experience working in government affairs, corporate affairs, public policy, or political environment (Capitol Hill, state house, trade association, consultancy, or corporate office). Familiarity with budget tracking and operational support systems (e.g., procurement platforms, expense tools). Demonstrated ability to work effectively with senior executives and external partners. Preferred Qualifications Experience working in government affairs, corporate affairs, public policy, or political environment (Capitol Hill, state house, trade association, consultancy, or corporate office). Familiarity with budget tracking and operational support systems (e.g., procurement platforms, expense tools). Demonstrated ability to work effectively with senior executives and external partners. Pay Range: $73,900.00 - $123,500.00 annually Starting rate of pay may vary based on factors including, but not limited to, position offered, location, education, training, and/or experience. For information regarding our benefit programs and eligibility, please visit https://talent.lowes.com/us/en/benefits . Associate Benefits ( https://talent.lowes.com/us/en/joining-our-team ) Working at one of the largest retail companies has its perks. We offer exceptional benefits and wellness programs for eligible full-time and part-time associates, tailored for many different lifestyles. Our benefits range from health, vision and dental insurance to paid vacation, tuition assistance and parental and family-building benefits. Plus, we offer learning and development opportunities to help our associates grow their skills and achieve their goals. Health, Dental and Vision insurance Life and Disability insurance Paid time off based on role, tenure, and locality, including vacation, holidays, sick and volunteer time Flexible spending and health savings accounts 401(k) Retirement account with company match Employee Assistance Program with concierge, work/life services and no-cost counseling for all kinds of needs Education support programs, including tuition assistance and trade skills scholarships Business Travel Accident insurance Maternity and Parental leave Adoption assistance Lowe's Associate Discount and broad discount platform Other discretionary benefits (based on eligibility) include annual bonuses, enrollment in Lowe's Employee Stock Purchase Plan and/or deferred compensation plan, and grant awards About Lowe’s Lowe’s Companies, Inc. (NYSE: LOW) is a FORTUNE® 100 home improvement company with total fiscal year 2025 sales of more than $86 billion. Lowe’s employs approximately 300,000 associates and operates over 1,750 home improvement stores, 540 branches and 120 distribution centers. Lowe’s is a core value S&P 500 equity stock and a dividend aristocrat. Based in Mooresville, N.C., Lowe’s supports the communities it serves through programs focused on creating safe, affordable housing, improving community spaces, helping to develop the next generation of skilled trade experts and providing disaster relief to communities in need. For more information, visit Lowes.com . Lowe’s is an equal opportunity employer and administers all personnel practices without regard to race, color, religious creed, sex, gender, age, ancestry, national origin, mental or physical disability or medical condition, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, military or veteran status, genetic information, or any other category protected under federal, state, or local law.

item.title: Summer Associate Internship Public Policy Assistant
item.description: Description The Summer Associate Program is a 12-week internship program beginning in May 2027 and ending in August 2027. Students will work on impactful projects and meaningful work during their internship. To qualify for this position, applicants must be currently pursuing a degree from an accredited college or university and have an anticipated graduation date of December 2027 or later. As part of Navy Federal's Military Affairs & Strategic Partnerships (MA&SP) department, GRPP collaborates closely with business units across the enterprise to assess policy implications, support strategic decision-making, and represent Navy Federal's interests before policymakers, regulators, trade associations, and other external stakeholders. The Public Policy Assistant Summer Associate will support the team's policy research, reporting, and operational activities. The associate will help maintain legislative, regulatory, stakeholder engagement, and project-tracking efforts that support the team's advocacy and strategic priorities. Responsibilities may include data analysis, reporting, process improvement, policy research, and the development of materials that help inform decision-making and increase visibility into GRPP activities across the enterprise. This role will provide exposure to public policy, government relations, stakeholder engagement, and cross-functional collaboration. Potential Projects Include: Support the collection, organization, and analysis of data related to legislative, regulatory, advocacy, stakeholder engagement, and project activities. Assist in preparing weekly, monthly, quarterly, and ad hoc reports, executive summaries, briefing materials, and presentations for senior leadership and internal stakeholders. Develop dashboards, reports, and visualizations that provide insights into policy developments, advocacy activities, stakeholder engagement, and team performance metrics. Support the tracking and management of team projects, action items, external engagements, and strategic initiatives to improve visibility and operational efficiency. Conduct research on federal and state legislative proposals, regulatory actions, and emerging public policy issues affecting credit unions, financial services, and military-affiliated communities. Perform industry benchmarking and trend analysis to support advocacy priorities and strategic planning efforts. Assist with preparing background materials, stakeholder summaries, and briefing documents for meetings with policymakers, regulators, trade associations, and internal business partners. Collaborate with business units across the enterprise to gather information and support policy-related initiatives and reporting. Complete a capstone project focused on improving GRPP's reporting, knowledge management, or operational processes, resulting in recommendations and tools that create long-term value for the team. Responsibilities Support the monitoring and tracking of legislative, regulatory, and public policy developments relevant to Navy Federal and the credit union industry. Conduct research and gather information from legislative, regulatory, industry, and internal sources to support policy analysis and advocacy efforts. Assist with maintaining records of team activities, stakeholder engagements, policy developments, and strategic initiatives. Compile, organize, and analyze data to support team reporting, metrics, and leadership updates. Prepare presentations, briefing materials, summaries, and reports for internal stakeholders and senior leadership. Support project management activities by tracking action items, milestones, and deliverables across multiple initiatives. Collaborate with business units and internal partners to collect information and support cross-functional projects. Help identify opportunities to improve team processes, reporting capabilities, and operational efficiency. Participate in team meetings, stakeholder engagements, and professional development activities to gain exposure to government relations and public policy functions. Qualifications Pursuing a degree in Public Policy, Political Science, Government, Public Administration, Economics, Business, Communications, Law, or a related field. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Ability to research, gather, and organize information from a variety of sources. Ability to manage multiple assignments and meet deadlines. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a team environment. Demonstrated interest in public policy, government, financial services, advocacy, or related fields. Desired Qualifications Coursework or project experience in Public Policy, Political Science, Government, Public Administration, Economics, Business, Communications, or a related field. Experience conducting research, analyzing information, or preparing reports and presentations through coursework, internships, student organizations, or other experiences. Familiarity with data analysis, reporting, data visualization, or business intelligence concepts. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Experience using Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint to organize information and communicate findings. Ability to synthesize complex information into concise summaries and recommendations. Experience balancing multiple projects, priorities, or extracurricular commitments. Interest in legislative affairs, regulatory issues, government relations, military affairs, consumer financial services, or the credit union industry. Demonstrated leadership through student organizations, volunteer activities, community involvement, athletics, military service, or other experiences. Additional Information Hours: Monday – Friday, 8:00 AM – 4:30 PM Location: 820 Follin Ln SE, Vienna, VA 22180

item.title: Legislative Analyst 9 P11 Departmental Analyst
item.description: Legislative Analyst 9-P11 (Departmental Analyst) State of Michigan Lansing, Michigan, United States Full-time 4 days ago $25.85 - $40.51 USD hourly Job Description The Department of Technology, Management and Budget supports the business operations of state agencies through a variety of services, including building management and maintenance, information technology, centralized contracting and procurement, budget and financial management, space planning and leasing, construction management, motor vehicle fleet operations, and oversight of the state retirement systems. The Legislative Analyst plays a key role within the DTMB Director's Office, supporting a department of nearly 3,000 public servants who deliver essential administrative services to all state government agencies. This role provides critical support to DTMB's legislative, engagement, and transparency functions while helping advance the department's mission and priorities. Working closely with the Legislative Director and Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Coordinator, this position analyzes legislation, coordinates legislative inquiries, researches and prepares policy analyses and correspondence, manages constituent requests, supports legislative hearings, and assists with the administration of DTMB's FOIA program. This position is responsible for constituent responses and for conducting in-depth research as needed to prepare DTMB leadership to advise on legislative strategy, or to prepare DTMB leadership to present to the legislature. The position collaborates extensively with DTMB leadership, state agencies, the Executive Office of the Governor, legislators, and external stakeholders to advance departmental priorities while promoting responsive, transparent, and effective government. Legislative Analyst - position description If you are a self-motivated person who wants a challenge and to work in a high paced environment, we are really interested in hearing from you. The state of Michigan offers a competitive work experience that includes a tuition reduction program at several key higher education institutes to help meet your educational and career goals. We offer health, life, dental vision, and disability insurances. Our employees enjoy paid parental leave, up to 9% match with 401(k), flexible spending accounts, excellent vacation and sick time policies, 14 holidays, and the ability to achieve work-life balance. Apply today to join the state of Michigan employee family! Required Education and Experience Education Possession of a bachelor's degree in any major. Experience Departmental Analyst 9 No specific type or amount is required. Departmental Analyst 10 One year of professional experience. Departmental Analyst P11 Two years of professional experience, including one year of experience equivalent to the intermediate (10) level in state service. Alternate Education and Experience Departmental Analyst 9 - 12 Educational level typically acquired through completion of high school and the equivalent of at least two years of full-time active-duty experience at or above the E-6 level in the uniformed services may be substituted for the education requirement. Additional Requirements and Information If applicable, attach copies of official college transcripts to your application. (Internet version of transcripts will not be accepted). Failure to attach applicable transcripts may result in your application being screened out. Your application for any position does not guarantee that you will be contacted by the Department/Agency for further consideration. Only those applicants interviewed will be notified of the results. The department reserves the right to close this posting prior to its original end date once a sufficient number of applications have been received. In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire. DTMB does not participate in STEM-OPT. View the job specification at: https://www.michigan.gov/mdcs/-/media/Project/Websites/mdcs/JOBSPECS/D/DepartmentalAnalyst.pdf Accommodations If you require a reasonable accommodation to participate in the application or selection processes, please contact the ADA coordinator for the agency that posted this position vacancy. Lansing, Michigan, United States $25.85 - $40.51 USD hourly

item.title: Human Resources Analyst Senior Election Commission
item.description: Position Description This is a Non-Civil Service position with the Election Commission. The Human Resources Analyst Senior is responsible for administering and coordinating the human resources functions of the Davidson County Election Commission. The analyst supports a professional, responsive, compliant, and service-oriented workplace by managing employee and election-worker personnel processes; coordinating with Metropolitan Government human resources, benefits, risk management, and other departments; maintaining confidential personnel records; monitoring required training; and assisting employees with leave, benefits, workplace concerns, and related matters. This position performs work requiring sound judgment, discretion, strong organizational skills, knowledge of applicable personnel policies and procedures, and the ability to manage high-volume hiring and personnel activity associated with elections. The analyst must maintain strict confidentiality and promote fair, respectful, and consistent personnel practices. *Note - A resume is required and must be attached to the application.* Typical Duties Employee Onboarding Coordinate onboarding for regular employees, temporary employees, election workers, and other personnel as assigned, including high-volume hiring and staffing needs during election cycles. Prepare, distribute, collect, and track new-hire documents and electronic forms, including documents processed through DocuSign or other approved systems. Enter and submit personnel information in Oracle or other designated systems for review and approval by Metropolitan Government Human Resources. Prepare and transmit required payroll paperwork and related personnel documentation to the Finance Manager. Monitor the status of new hires and ensure that all required human resources and payroll approvals are completed in a timely manner, so personnel are ready to work as scheduled. Establish and maintain accurate, complete, and confidential personnel files in accordance with applicable records retention requirements and personnel policies. Coordinate personnel actions involving Election Commissioners, including onboarding, separation, and related administrative processing when Commission membership changes. Personnel Administration and Records Process and track personnel actions, including promotions, demotions, transfers, resignations, retirements, terminations, changes in employment status, and other employment-related updates. Ensure personnel transactions are accurately entered into Oracle or other authorized systems and are properly documented, approved, and communicated to applicable departments. Maintain current employee data, including emergency contact information, and support the maintenance of contact information for election workers when assigned. Respond promptly and accurately to unemployment-related requests, including requests from Metropolitan Government Human Resources, unemployment vendors, and other authorized parties, while meeting required response deadlines. Prepare reports, correspondence, records, and documentation related to human resources functions as requested. Employee Relations, Leave, Benefits, and Support Serve as a primary resource for employees and managers, providing timely guidance on personnel policies, benefits, leave options, workplace resources, and appropriate administrative processes. Assist employees with Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), family leave, and other leave-related matters, coordinating with Metropolitan Government Human Resources and other departments as appropriate. Provide employees with information about the Employee Assistance Program (EAP), benefits, and available support resources, particularly when employees are experiencing personal or workplace difficulties. Maintain confidentiality and exercise sensitivity when responding to employee concerns, personal matters, medical information, leave requests, and workplace issues. Support fair and consistent application of personnel policies and escalate complex employee relations matters to the Administrator of Elections, Metropolitan Government Human Resources, legal counsel, or other appropriate authorities. Training, Compliance, and Policy Administration Monitor compliance with Metropolitan Government, State of Tennessee, and Election Commission training requirements. Maintain working knowledge of mandatory training requirements and develop or maintain systems to track employee completion and outstanding training obligations. Review employee training transcripts periodically, notify employees and supervisors of incomplete requirements, and assign training through Oracle or other approved systems when appropriate. Coordinate and document Title VI training and compliance activities as required by the State of Tennessee or other applicable authorities. Maintain and update Election Commission personnel policies and procedures in coordination with the Administrator of Elections, Metropolitan Government Human Resources, legal counsel, and other appropriate parties. Attend and share information with Senior Leadership team from scheduled human resources meetings, including quarterly meetings and other required professional development or compliance meetings. Safety, Emergency, and Risk Management Support Coordinate Injury on Duty claims and related paperwork; communicate with employees, supervisors, risk management personnel, and other relevant parties to support timely processing and follow-up. Assist in maintaining the Election Commission’s emergency plan and personnel emergency contact procedures. Support election-related continuity planning, including readiness of staff and, when assigned, election workers for emergency communications and operational needs. Budget and Election Operations Support Work collaboratively with the Finance Manager on human resources matters that may affect staffing costs, payroll, benefits, position control, budget planning, and election-related personnel expenditures. Perform special projects, election-related assignments, and other duties as assigned by the Administrator of Elections. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in human resources, public administration, business administration, management, or a closely related field from an accredited college or university; and at least three years of progressively responsible human resources, personnel administration, payroll, benefits, employee relations, or public-sector administrative experience. * Additional experience may be considered in lieu of education (1:1 ratio)* Candidates with accreditations earned in a foreign institute are encouraged to apply. Note: Per Metro Ordinance No. SO94-1078. All employees of the Metropolitan Government shall be residents of the State of Tennessee or become residents of the state within six (6) months of employment as a prerequisite to employment with the Metropolitan Government. Preferred Experience, Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Human resources experience in a governmental, public-sector, or highly regulated environment. Experience with high-volume or seasonal hiring, onboarding, and personnel tracking. Experience using Oracle Human Capital Management, Oracle Enterprise Resource Planning, or a comparable human resources information system. Experience coordinating FMLA, workers’ compensation or Injury on Duty claims, unemployment responses, payroll-related paperwork, and mandatory training compliance. Professional human resources certification, such as SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, PHR, SPHR, IPMA-HR, or equivalent credential. Knowledge of election administration, election worker recruitment, or election operations. We are an equal opportunity employer. All individuals, regardless of personal characteristics, are encouraged to apply. Metro Nashville is committed to selecting the most qualified candidate for each of our roles. Metro Nashville Government respects the religious beliefs and practices of all employees and will make, on request, an accommodation for such observances when a reasonable accommodation is available that does not create an undue hardship on business operations. Requests for ADA or other protected accommodations for the recruitment process should be directed to the Davidson County Election Commission at (615) 862-8800.

item.title: Legislative Coordinator
item.description: The work we do matters! Hiring Agency: Revenue - Agency 16 Location: Lincoln, NE Hiring Rate: $26.395 Job Posting: JR2026-00029453 Legislative Coordinator (Open) Applications No Longer Accepted On (If no date is displayed, job is posted as open until closed): 10-08-2026 Job Description: Under administrative direction, this position is responsible for the coordination, the drafting, submission, and monitoring of legislation both within the Nebraska Department of Revenue (DOR) and external bodies such as the Governor’s Policy Research Office. Provides political analysis and strategies for communicating the agency position to external parties; performs related work as assigned. Job duties include: 1. Communicating the positions of the DOR on pending Legislation. 2. Communicating the position of the DOR on other issues. 3. Advocating for the DOR’s and the Administration’s positions. 4. Researching, reviewing and drafting legislation. 5. Maintaining accurate information on the current status of each bill and notifies agency administrative and/or program officials when action or attention is required. 6. Coordinating a legislative tracking system and reviewing Fiscal Notes on legislation. 7. Responding to inquiries from the press, legislature, and others on a variety of issues. 8. Researching issues for legislation, taxpayer guidance, or other response. 9. Reviewing forms, policies and other documents. 10. Serving as the DOR Public Information Officer. Requirements / Qualifications: Minimum Qualifications: Post high school coursework or training in public relations/public affairs, communications, political science, or public administration and experience in policy development and implementation or assisting in drafting bills, researching statutes, and revision of rules/regulations. Knowledge of: the legislative process; interrelationship of various statutes; principles of administrations such as planning, organization, evaluation, analysis, evaluation, communication theory, and techniques of public relations. Ability to: effectively present positions and initiatives to third parties; develop strategies; research and interpret and apply federal/state policies/procedures; develop and implement policies and procedures; effectively communicate orally and in writing; facilitate consensus building and conflict resolution; and organize multiple priorities. item.title: Economic Policy Program Fall Internship
item.description: BPC's Spring Internship Program The Bipartisan Policy Center’s internship program is built around each intern’s goals. Interns conduct research, support project analysts and staff, and see firsthand how people from both parties work together on policy. The program also offers exposure to the policymaking process and the functions of a think tank, plus professional development and networking with BPC staff and interns across DC. Spring interns work 18 to 20 hours per week and receive a $3,000 stipend, paid in two equal installments during the internship. Interns set a weekly schedule with their intern manager at the start of the semester and can adjust it around class commitments. BPC’s internships are based in our Washington, DC office. BPC staff are in the office Tuesday through Thursday, with the option to work from home on Monday and Friday. Relocation assistance is not provided. The Spring 2027 internship program runs Tuesday, January 26, 2027, through Thursday, April 1, 2027. Project Description: BPC's Economic Policy Program (EPP) develops bipartisan policy recommendations designed to enhance the economic opportunity, prosperity, and security of the American people. EPP continues to be a trusted leader in the analysis of federal fiscal policy, encompassing the areas of debt, tax reform, sequestration, the federal budget process, and retirement and financial security. EPP’s is known for its analysis of the federal debt limit, a project that was initially led by now Federal Reserve Chairman Jay Powell during his time as a Fellow at BPC. Subsequent analyses have long been widely cited both in the media and directly by policymakers. Our team also provides research, analysis, and commentary on the major fiscal and budget debates occurring at any given time in Washington, from the implementation of the Fiscal Responsibility Act’s spending caps to the risks and harms of government shutdowns to the future trajectory of U.S. government finances. EPP’s tax portfolio seeks bipartisan reform that will create opportunities for businesses of all sizes, support workers and families, and improve our nation’s fiscal outlook in the years to come. We are especially focused on opportunities for fiscally responsible tax reform. Our work on retirement security focuses on policies that expand access to well-designed retirement savings vehicles, help Americans preserve their retirement income, and resolve Social Security’s structural imbalance to avoid harmful and abrupt benefit cuts when the program’s trust fund is depleted. We continue to play a prominent role in informing and promoting legislative progress on private-sector savings, working to advance reforms that help Americans create financial security through emergency savings accounts, savings for retirement, and other government assistance to promote economic growth and security. In 2022, EPP acquired and relaunched the American Savings Education Council (ASEC), a unique cross-sector public-private partnership originally formed in 1994 by the U.S. Department of Labor and Employee Benefit Research Institute. Responsibilities: The intern will be working closely with all the policy experts across our team, reporting to the program manager. Responsibilities will vary day-to-day, but may include: Support long-term policy projects and papers by conducting background research and writing Draft blog posts and assist staff in preparing responses to Hill and media requests Monitoring major congressional activity, analyzing budget documents Take notes at Congressional hearings and external events Event planning, program management, and administrative tasks Eligibility: Undergraduate students at the rising junior level or above, currently enrolled graduate students, or graduates within the past 12 months Non-U.S. citizens are eligible to apply but must have a valid work permit or visa verifying eligibility to work in the United States. BPC does not offer visa sponsorship. Qualifications: Must be an enrolled in an undergraduate, graduate school or be a recent graduate Strong research and writing skills Ability to communicate clearly and effectively An interest in fiscal and economic policy topics, such as tax policy, retirement savings, and federal budget policy Strong research and data analysis skills; proficiency with Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Suite preferred Application Process: Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until a qualified candidate has been identified . Send a separate application for each internship of interest, and do not submit more than once to the same posting. Incomplete applications will not be considered. No phone calls, please. Required Materials (if possible, please submit as one PDF file): Resume Cover letter Writing sample, three to five pages College or university transcript (unofficial is acceptable) Brief response to the question “What does bipartisanship mean to you?” (five to eight sentences) To celebrate diversity and ensure equity and inclusivity, BPC is committed to: Recruiting and retaining a diverse workforce with insights and solutions for our increasingly divided society Creating a workplace culture where all employees feel valued and their perspectives are heard Developing policy solutions and undertaking research that reflect a diversity of thought and experience These commitments help us fulfill our mission and foster bipartisanship more effectively.

item.title: Herdsperson 2 Gilt Selection
item.description: If you are currently employed at Smithfield, please log into Workday and submit your application through the Jobs Hub. Have a seat at our table. When you join Smithfield, you become part of something special – a company that's sustainably feeding people around the world, producing good food the right way with respect for our people, animals, communities and planet. With opportunities across locations and functions, a culture grounded in our Core Four values - gratitude, communication, respect and accountability - and a strong commitment to learning, collaboration, and innovation, Smithfield offers challenging and rewarding careers where you can grow, contribute and make a real impact. Apply Now! Your Opportunity Compensation $17.75; Drivers License & Good Driving Record REQUIRED! The Herdsperson assists other Herd Technicians in routine animal care and general farm tasks to ensure the welfare/well-being of the animals. Employee may operate mowers, tractors, trucks, bus, and other farm equipment as directed. May be in training for advanced Herd Technician designation. The Herdsperson position will also provide for the care of all animals at the designated work site, particularly their health, growth, and breeding. Core Responsibilities Feeds, waters, vaccinates, and performs general animal husbandry tasks including basic veterinary procedures. Maintains flexibility with a willingness to change plans according to the direction of farm leadership. Assists in moving animals and maintaining efficient animal flows. Sanitizes and washes multiple areas on the farm using high pressure equipment. Processes piglets, which includes injecting medications, castrating, docking tails, and ear notching. Maintains accurate production information and update all department records as required. Treats sick animals with a variety of pharmaceuticals by injection, oral application, and/or other methods as required. Follows the Standard Operation Procedures, Production Manuals, or Appropriate Training Guides as required. Assists with facility and equipment maintenance. Assists with maintaining barn, office cleanliness, and laundry duties. Follows the Company’s animal welfare policies and procedures including: providing a physical environment that meets the animal’s needs, providing access to adequate water and high quality feed, providing humane treatment of the animals, providing identification and appropriate treatment of animals in need of health care and following the guidelines for euthanasia. - Responsible for complying with all environmental, safety and biosecurity laws and procedures. The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this job. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of personnel so classified. May perform other duties as assigned. Qualifications To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals to perform the essential functions. High School diploma or GED preferred. Previous livestock handing helpful. Valid state driver’s license with acceptable driving record (depending on location). Ability to do hard physical labor. Strong commitment to teamwork. Willingness to shower daily in and out of facility. Ability to follow instructions and deal with standardized situations. Must be able to work an average 48-hour work week, which can vary frequently. Weekend, evening, and holiday work required as needed. Must be on call for emergency situations to include but not limit to, power outages or personnel shortages. Ability to work well with others in fast paced, dynamic environment. Ability to be respectful, approachable and team oriented while building strong working relationships and a positive work environment. Work Environment & Physical Demands The work environment characteristics & physical demands described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Vision abilities include close vision, distance vision and ability to adjust focus. Occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 lbs. Frequently required to stand; walk; use hands to handle or feel; reach with hands and arms; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl and talk or hear. Must be able to work with and around a wide range of antibiotics (i.e. penicillin). Must be able to tolerate blood, animal dander, manure, dust, odors, and frequently noisy conditions. Relocation Package Available No EEO Information Smithfield is an equal opportunity employer committed to workplace diversity. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, age, gender identity, protected veterans status, status as a disabled individual or any other protected group status or non-job characteristic as directed by law. If you are an individual with a disability and would like to request a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment selection process, please call us at 757-357-1595.

item.title: Government Affairs Manager
item.description: This position requires occasional evening and weekend work. POSITION SUMMARY: The Government Affairs Manager is responsible for strategically identifying and building critical relationships with state government officials and guiding staff interactions with county and city government officials. This role proactively develops collaborative relationships with organizations working on factors that drive food insecurity to further Houston Food Bank’s vision of “a world that doesn’t need food banks.” This position researches and analyzes policies, communicates this information to internal and external stakeholders, and assists staff in creating opportunities to enhance the community’s advocacy skills so they can provide input to policymakers. This role is also responsible for preparing issue briefs, testimony, talking points, presentations, and other appropriate communiques to inform the community and elected officials. The Government Affairs Manager assists during times of disaster as a liaison between government entities and HFB departments and will be periodically called upon to share talking points with media. Adhere to PACT values. (Purpose: Using our strengths passionately to contribute to our mission. Accountability: Choosing to rise above one’s circumstances and demonstrating ownership to achieve results. See It. Own It. Solve It. Do It. Courage: Standing up for what’s right and acting. Transparency: Doing things openly and honestly). ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS: 1.Builds Relationships with State Government Officials. Serves as a liaison to state government officials and their staff for areas served directly by HFB and through its partner organizations. Assists in connecting state government officials with HFB or community stakeholders/resources that can meet the needs of their constituents. Works with elected offices to arrange tours of HFB and HFB partner organizations. Maintains a database of government officials and their staff and inputs significant touchpoints to track metrics. Provides state government officials with information pertinent to their constituents, including data on food insecurity, HFB partners in their district/precinct, pounds of food distributed, etc. 2.Researches and analyzes policies that impact Houston Food Bank Affiliates, HFB partner organizations, and their clients, and communicates this information to internal and external stakeholders. Researches and tracks information from various sources and stakeholders that could impact HFB’s operations or its client populations and reports this information to government officials. Identifies opportunities for local government funding that would support HFB’s work and clients. Tracks and reports on state election cycles. Works with HFB Marketing and Communications Department and other Houston Food Bank staff to maintain and update content for the Action Center and advocacy webpage, including updated data on hunger and poverty, calls to action, and advocacy alerts on pertinent policy and legislation. Works collaboratively with other HFB departments to understand the experience of HFB operations and programs and translates policy and government insights for HFB leadership. 3.Works with key stakeholders to elicit input on systems change and creates opportunities to enhance their advocacy skills and provide input to policymakers. Collaborates with HFB staff who interact with community members to identify and train client advocates and creates opportunities for community dialogue about hunger and poverty-related challenges and potential systemic solutions. Provides advocacy training for partner organizations. Maintains consistent communication with HFB partner organizations to identify policy solutions that further HFB’s vision of “a world that doesn’t need food banks.” 4.Provides leadership for local government and community relations initiatives, overseeing engagement with local government officials, community organizations, and key stakeholders to advance organizational priorities, expand funding opportunities, influence public policy, and strengthen community partnerships that support the organization's mission 5.Collaborates with Houston Food Bank’s state association, Feeding Texas, and other food banks across the state in advancing the organization’s state legislative agenda. Works with Houston Food Bank staff and other organizations to create our legislative agenda and successfully drive it through the state legislative process. Regularly participates in statewide coalition meetings to stay aware of policy recommendations and changes. Develops advocacy campaigns to support the advancement of HFB’s legislative agenda. 6.Assists the Government Relations senior leadership in serving as a disaster liaison to government entities. Maintains up-to-date knowledge of resources and needs of internal and external stakeholders through consistent communication with state elected officials and other stakeholders as identified by the Government Relations senior leadership. Ensures factors necessary for successful implementation of Government Relations Department COOP are in place and can be executed during times of disaster. SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES: Manage one (1) or more direct reports by providing guidance and/or oversight to employees and/or contractors. Develops and maintains roles, responsibilities, and expectations. Practices performance management in support of employee development and performs administrative duties associated with being a people manager. Responsibilities include interviewing, planning, assigning, directing work, and resolving problems. Responsibilities also include sponsoring and participating in and/or supporting project teams sponsored by other management team members. QUALIFICATIONS: Education/Experience: Bachelor's degree from an accredited four-year college or university in Political Science, Public Affairs, or a closely related field 3-5 years of related experience in strategic interaction with elected officials 3-5 years in public policy or related work 2-3 years of management experience with direct reports Experience giving presentations and preparing memos, reports, and essays using proper punctuation, spelling, and grammar Bilingual: speak and write in Spanish, Mandarin/Chinese, Vietnamese, or other language preferred Certificates, Licenses, and Registrations: Must have reliable transportation, a valid driver’s license, and insurance. item.title: Research And Legislative Analyst
item.description: Research and Legislative Analyst Come join a team where you will be valued while engaging in meaningful work supporting the cities and towns in South Carolina! Flexible/hybrid remote work arrangements available after a training and orientation period. Who We Are Welcome to the Municipal Association of South Carolina. The Association is a nonprofit organization representing all of South Carolina’s 271 cities and towns. The Association is dedicated to the principles established by the cities and towns that founded it: to offer the services, programs and products that will give municipal officials the knowledge, experience and tools necessary to operate efficiently and effectively in the complex world of local government. The Association’s staff works as a team to deliver top-notch customer service to thousands of municipal officials across the state. From the largest cities to small, rural towns, we strive to offer trainings, grants, risk management services, statewide legislative advocacy, resources and other services that help municipal officials govern smarter and better. South Carolina hometowns, represented by the Municipal Association of South Carolina, bring value to our state as important building blocks in supporting economic growth and prosperity. Come be a part of the team. To learn more about the Municipal Association and its programs and services, visit www.masc.sc . What We’re Searching For The Municipal Association of SC is accepting applications for the position of research and legislative analyst. This full-time position will gather, analyze and interpret data to influence public policy related to municipal government and determine the impact current issues, new policies, and government regulations may have on municipalities using both quantitative and qualitative analyses. This position reports to the director of advocacy. Job Duties: Develops, coordinates, and promotes the Association’s research activities, including conducting studies, developing research reports, and responding to general requests for information. Conducts quantitative and qualitative research and prepares reports on various topics related to municipal governance and operations and legislative issues affecting cities. Selects appropriate software for the analysis of and presentation of data and information. Develops, implements and manages polling activities in support of municipal issues. This includes, but is not limited to, solicitation and management of outside polling firms, development of poll questions and analysis and reporting of poll results to anyone with an interest in municipal government. Develops, implements and manages special projects that are analytical by nature and related to municipal issues; uses software to build and maintain databases that gather and analyze data; draws conclusions from analyses and summarizes conclusions for use by legislators, municipal officials, Association staff and others with an interest in municipal government. Plays a role in positioning the Municipal Association as the primary resource for accurate and timely information about municipal operations and services. Analyzes state and federal legislation for impact on municipalities and provides updates for various parties as appropriate. Analyzes and explains the impact of existing and proposed legislation to municipal officials and others as required. Provides training to municipal staff and elected officials through the Association’s affiliate associations and institutes. Conducts training for municipal councils on specific topics upon request. Maintains knowledge of current municipal issues; attends local, state and regional meetings; communicates with co-workers and professional peers to stay informed of municipal issues. Assists with the development and implementation of Association workshops and regional meetings. Receives and responds to inquiries, requests for assistance and concerns in areas of responsibility. Attends meetings, technical or professional seminars, and conferences to enhance job knowledge and skills. Travels periodically in state and infrequently out of state to perform the duties of this position. Performs all other duties as assigned. Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in political science, public administration, urban studies, city planning, statistics, information science, or other related field. Advanced degree in public administration or political science preferred. Minimum of three years of experience in research in local or state government operations and/or policy development. Advanced experience in Microsoft Excel and database management is required. Must possess a valid South Carolina driver’s license Skilled in conducting research, collecting data, performing data analysis, and reporting research findings. Excellent written and oral communication skills; strong interpersonal and analytical skills; and the ability to think strategically and work as a team player. Pay info: Competitive salary based on qualifications and excellent benefits package including South Carolina State Retirement and insurance How to apply: Visit the Municipal Association of SC Career Center . The Municipal Association of South Carolina is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

item.title: Vice President Government Affairs
item.description: For 75 years, Charles River employees have worked together to assist in the discovery, development and safe manufacture of new drug therapies. When you join our family, you will have a significant impact on the health and well-being of people across the globe. Whether your background is in life sciences, finance, IT, sales or another area, your skills will play an important role in the work we perform. In return, we’ll help you build a career that you can feel passionate about. Job Overview BASIC SUMMARY: The VP of Federal Government Affairs will serve as a key advocate for the Charles River’s interests before federal policymakers, with a primary focus on drug development issues. This individual will develop and execute education and advocacy strategies, engage with congressional offices and federal agencies, manage third-party lobbyists, and help shape policy outcomes that support the Charles River's strategic objectives. The role requires strong policy acumen, exceptional relationship‑building abilities, and the capacity to translate complex business issues into clear and compelling public‑policy positions. The ideal candidate is a self-starter who thrives in a fast‑paced, highly collaborative environment and brings deep experience working within the federal legislative and regulatory landscape. The ideal candidate will blend visionary leadership with a hands-on approach to advance the organization's mission and shape critical legislative outcomes. Job Description ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Duty % of Time Spent (no less than 10%) Strategic Policy Development & Vision: Design and execute comprehensive federal government strategies that align with the organization's purpose and goals. Assess the impact of legislative or regulatory proposals, and establish short- and long-term policy priorities. Lead direct advocacy efforts with congressional staff, elected officials, and federal regulators on issues impacting Charles River 25% Stakeholder Engagement & Coalition Building: Cultivate and maintain strategic relationships with key government officials, lawmakers, industry partners, and advocacy groups. Build and lead high-impact coalitions to amplify the organization's voice and drive consensus on critical policy issues. Monitors the legislative and regulatory environment and communicates developments to Charles RIver stakeholders 20% Advocacy & Government Relations: Direct third-party lobbying activities and grassroots advocacy and education efforts to advance or oppose specific legislation and regulations. Prepare compelling testimony, policy briefs, and advocacy campaigns designed to influence policymakers and key regulatory bodies. 20% Board Communication & Organizational Leadership: Serve as the primary subject matter expert on all federal issues and support the Chief Legal Officer and Chief Communications Officer in thier support of, and education to, the Board of Directors on these matters. Translate complex political, economic, and social issues into actionable updates, ensuring the board is informed of emerging risks and opportunities. 15% Research Analysis & Impact: Oversee the data collection, research, and rigorous evaluation of public policy outcomes. Ensure all policy positions are backed by evidence and measure the effectiveness of advocacy initiatives to demonstrate value to stakeholders 10% Budget & Resource Management: Develop and manage the annual budget for the public policy department. Allocate necessary resources for policy research, lobbying efforts, and public awareness campaigns while ensuring strict compliance with lobbying and financial disclosure regulations 5% Stakeholders include Chief Communications Officer, Chief Scientific Officer, CEO. Compensation Data The hiring range for this position in the US is $250,000/yr - $280,000/yr. Please note that salaries vary within the range based on factors including, but not limited to, experience, skills, education, certifications, location and any collective agreements, if applicable. Job Requirements MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: Education: Master’s degree in public policy, Political Science, Public Administration, Law or related field, o r advanced scientific degrees in the field Experience: 10+ years of progressive experience in public policy, government relations, or legislative advocacy. Preferably in a publicly-traded company. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be accepted as a satisfactory substitute for the specific education and experience listed above. Other: 5+years in a senior leadership position or a position that interacts with Board of Directors and Executive Leadership roles. Deep understanding of local, state and federal legislative and regulatory processes Proven track record of successfully building coalitions and influencing public policy outcomes. Exceptional written communications skills for drafting briefs, testimonies and board reports Strong media literacy and experience serving as an official organizational spokesperson WORKPLACE REQUIREMENTS: Lives and located in Washington D.C As a remote worker, has sufficient internet and technical infrastructure and a home-based location suitable for creating a professional environment for video conference calls. About Corporate Functions The Corporate Functions provide operational support across Charles River in areas such as Human Resources, Finance, IT, Legal, Sales, Quality Assurance, Marketing, and Corporate Development. They partner with their colleagues across the company to develop and drive strategies and to set global standards. The functions are essential to providing a bridge between strategic vision and operational readiness, to ensure ongoing functional innovation and capability improvement. About Charles River Charles River is an early-stage contract research organization (CRO). We have built upon our foundation of laboratory animal medicine and science to develop a diverse portfolio of discovery and safety assessment services, both Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) and non-GLP, to support clients from target identification through preclinical development. Charles River also provides a suite of products and services to support our clients’ clinical laboratory testing needs and manufacturing activities. Utilizing this broad portfolio of products and services enables our clients to create a more flexible drug development model, which reduces their costs, enhances their productivity and effectiveness to increase speed to market. With over 20,000 employees within 110 facilities in over 20 countries around the globe, we are strategically positioned to coordinate worldwide resources and apply multidisciplinary perspectives in resolving our client’s unique challenges. Our client base includes global pharmaceutical companies, biotechnology companies, government agencies and hospitals and academic institutions around the world. At Charles River, we are passionate about our role in improving the quality of people’s lives. Our mission, our excellent science and our strong sense of purpose guide us in all that we do, and we approach each day with the knowledge that our work helps to improve the health and well-being of many across the globe. We have proudly worked on 80% of the drugs approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in the past five years. We’re committed to providing benefits that elevate your quality of life. Based on your position these may include: bonus/incentives based on performance, 401K, paid time off, stock purchase program, Health and wellness coverage, employee and family wellbeing support programs, and work life balance flexibility. item.title: Coordinator Government Affairs
item.description: Description GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES The Public Policy Team works to protect our state’s business climate and regional reputation by supporting key policies at the state and local levels that affect metro Atlanta's economy, talent, and community. The Coordinator role on the Government Affairs team will assist the Public Policy team with legislative tracking, research, administrative tasks, attending and summarizing legislative meetings, monitoring activities at various levels of government, attending and representing the chamber at various meetings, and other tasks as assigned. The Coordinator will report to the Manager of Government Affairs, while collaborating with all Public Policy team members and departments at the chamber. Preferred skills for this role include an understanding of the legislative process and an eagerness for continued growth, the ability to manage multiple responsibilities, strong attention to detail, and the ability to communicate professionally to ensure MAC's success in the public policy sphere. Our ideal candidate is a high-achiever, self-starter, and team player with an interest in deepening their understanding of Georgia’s political landscape and policy skills. Successful candidates will be organized, possess strong networking and communication skills, and demonstrate the ability to manage multiple projects without constant supervision. DAY-TO-DAY DUTIES INCLUDE: Legislative Develop a strong understanding of MAC’s legislative priorities, and work alongside team members to craft strategies and tactics to implement key priorities Monitor, research, and track in real-time legislative activity at the state and local government levels that could impact Georgia and the metro Atlanta region Assist with scheduling and executing meetings with elected officials, executive and legislative staff, business and civic community partners, coalitions, and key stakeholders Manage team-specific documents and resources that are critical to the team's operations and performance at the state capitol Conduct research and prepare policy summaries, briefing forms, talking points, letters of support, etc. Interact wit h federal, state, and local elected officials, department and agency leads, and their staff Assist with coalition building and stakeholder outreach around key legislative priorities Support and assist with the biennial development of the Metro Atlanta Chamber’s policy agenda and legislative priorities Build relationships with key campaign, fundraising, and political staff members Attend outside meetings, conferences, legislative functions, and other job-related events as directed. Administrative Manage accounting, budgeting, financial oversight, and reporting for Metro Atlanta Chamber Political Action Committee (MACPAC) Plan and execute administrative tasks for political entities including accounting, budgeting, financial oversight, ethics reporting, scheduling, communications, etc. Oversee operations of various entities, including fundraising, consultant management and oversight, board communications, ethics reporting, compliance, etc. Coordinate and execute the public policy team's state-mandated ethics reporting Event and Communications Support Assist with planning and execution of chamber events, meetings, initiatives, and other policy events attended by investors, elected officials, staff, and partners. Coordinate and draft internal and external updates on chamber priorities and key legislation Assist with creating department communications, social media, website/blog content, etc. External Foster relationships with MAC members, business community partners, lobbyists, government officials, and government staff Plan and execute meetings with elected officials and staff outside of the metro Atlanta region Perform other duties as assigned. QUALIFICATIONS: One to three years of experience preferred in government affairs, public policy, executive or legislative branch, community affairs, non-profit advocacy, regulatory affairs, or political campaigns Familiarity with the legislative process and Georgia’s political landscape, along with a continued eagerness to grow Ability to quickly synthesize legislation, regulations, data, and strategies, and to communicate them to team members and senior leaders Exceptional attention to detail, organizational skills, and verbal and written communication skills Excellent social and interpersonal skills; capacity to interact with a wide variety of people in government, politics, and civic and business leadership Ability to quickly identify barriers to success and devise strategies or tactics to remove or mitigate them Ability to maintain a non-partisan approach in all respects, work with all members of the executive departments and agencies, and the General Assembly and their staffs Self-starter, capable of working both independently and collaboratively with other team members to produce desired outcomes High energy, versatile, and able to multitask; flexible, able to adapt to changing priorities and plans Qualifications The Metro Atlanta Chamber (MAC) serves as a catalyst for a more prosperous and vibrant metro Atlanta. To advance economic growth and improve our quality of place, MAC is focused on starting, growing, and recruiting companies to our 29-county region. We're also focused on growing our innovation economy by promoting and strengthening connections to drive Atlanta's innovation and entrepreneurial culture. MAC is committed to being an active voice for the business community, serving as an advocate for a competitive business climate, advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion as economic imperatives, and telling Atlanta's story. Our Purpose, Principles, and Core Values MAC's purpose is to UNLEASH ATLANTA'S AMBITION, and in doing so we embody the following principles: Sit Down Together, Stand Up to Act Knock Down Walls, Open Doors Take the Lead, Share the Credit Sharpen the Focus, Expand the Reach At MAC, we naturally exhibit an unwavering commitment to three core values: to be relentless, smart, and all-in . This means every team member is: Relentless . MAC employees take pride in being relentless with an unwavering focus. Our partners trust us to deliver on our commitments. There isn't room for cutting corners, being aimless, or rejecting change. We are bold and persistent and execute with innovation and edge. Smart . Team members at MAC know that intense curiosity allows us to grow. We leverage instinct, integrity, and data to drive our strategy and achieve our purpose. As problem-solving idea generators, we have a natural advantage in any challenge. All-In. We're a greater force when we rally together. It doesn't matter what our title or position is: we trust each other and work as one to multiply our collective impact and achieve ambitious goals.

item.title: Director Of Legislative Affairs
item.description: Introduction The Director of Legislative Affairs reports to the Chief of Staff and serves as a direct manager for legislative aides, senior legislative aides, and certain legislative fellows, in coordination with the Policy Director and other senior staff as appropriate. The Director mentors staff, identifies learning gaps, supports recruitment and retention, and helps maintain a strong internal staff pipeline for the caucus and state government. The position plays a central role in onboarding, training, performance review, staff support, and early dispute resolution. As part of the staff mission of supporting legislators and the public, the Director, in coordination with the Chief of Staff and Deputy Chief of Staff, is expected to act as a short-term backstop in situations where Legislative aide performance is unable to meet the needs of their legislator or their constituents. The Director is expected to maintain regular communication with members and staff, assess whether staff assignments are meeting member needs, and address concerns before they become larger operational problems. In coordination with the Chief of Staff and Deputy Chief of Staff, the Director also helps manage formal staff feedback systems, including annual performance evaluations, staff check-ins, and annual staff surveys designed to identify operational concerns, training needs, and opportunities to improve caucus support. Summary Statement The Director of Legislative Affairs is a senior caucus staff position responsible for legislative operations, committee management, staff development, stakeholder coordination, and strategic support for the House Majority Caucus. The Director supports the Chief of Staff, Speaker, leadership team, members, legislative staff, fellows, and policy staff to ensure legislative work, constituent services, committee coverage, and internal operations are coordinated, professional, and responsive. The role requires strong judgment, discretion, staff-management experience, knowledge of state government, and the ability to manage complex assignments in a fast-paced legislative environment. The Director is expected to anticipate issues, resolve problems early, and strengthen caucus systems, staff culture, and external relationships. Essential Functions 1. Staff Management, Mentorship, and Culture • Supervise, support, and mentor legislative aides, senior legislative aides, and assigned legislative fellows in coordination with the Chief of Staff, Policy Director, and other senior staff. • Conduct standing meetings, organic check-ins, and performance reviews with staff and elected members to assess staff needs, identify concerns, and support professional growth. • Help recruit, interview, hire, onboard, train, and support legislative staff and fellows, including participation in dispute processes and succession planning when needed. • Promote recruitment and retention by strengthening staff culture, supporting future planning for staff, and maintaining positive relationships with staff who move into other roles in state government or related fields. • Develop or update guidance documents, onboarding materials, training resources, and internal processes to fill learning gaps, especially for newer staff. • Coordinate the annual staff survey process with the Chief of Staff and Deputy Chief of Staff, including developing questions, encouraging candid feedback, reviewing results, identifying trends, and recommending improvements to caucus operations, communication, training, morale, and staff support. • Oversee the annual staff performance evaluation process in partnership with the Chief of Staff and Deputy Chief of Staff, including collecting member feedback, reviewing staff input where appropriate, identifying strengths and areas for improvement, and assisting with follow-up meetings, coaching conversations, or performance plans. 2. Committee Management and Legislative Operations • Lead coordination of the committee schedule, committee planning, room assignments, agenda requests, meeting preparation, and related logistics in partnership with the Policy Director, policy analysts, legislative aides, and other staff. • Ensure committee-related information is shared with the appropriate members and staff in a timely, organized, and useful manner. • Synthesize notable committee actions, testimony, member comments, stakeholder concerns, amendments, and emerging issues for the Chief of Staff and leadership. • Coordinate with policy staff on committee work assigned to legislative fellows and ensure fellows receive appropriate guidance and oversight. • Continue to improve and refine House committee operations process through each successive session of the General Assembly. 3. Member Support and Constituent Issue Resolution • Maintain open communication with legislators to assess whether staff assignments, constituent work, committee coverage, and district support are meeting member needs. • Assist in resolving member concerns involving legislative aides, senior legislative aides, fellows, agency responsiveness, constituent matters, or committee support. • Work with individual constituents, constituent groups, community organizations, and public agencies to gather information, resolve conflicts, present issues, or disseminate information when appropriate. • Identify recurring district or constituent issues and elevate patterns to members, senior staff, policy staff, or leadership. • Serve as a backstop for situations where staff are unable to meet the needs of their members and their constituents. 4. Policy, Stakeholder, and Strategic & Support • Provide accurate and timely research, recommendations, and background information on legislative issues and proposals. • Engage stakeholders, legislators, agencies, and outside partners on policy initiatives and caucus priorities. • Work with the Communications Director and communications staff to support messaging plans for legislation, caucus initiatives, and special projects. • Provide research and consultation to leadership and members on administrative, operational, procedural, or policy issues affecting the caucus. • Develop tactics and strategies that respond to changing priorities, member needs, legislative dynamics, and emerging challenges. 5. Training, External Relationships and Governmental Liaison Work • Develop and manage training opportunities for legislative aides, senior legislative aides, fellows, and senior staff with outside partners such as NCSL, CSG, state agencies, the Governor's Office, the judicial branch, community organizations, nonprofits, and other relevant partners. • Serve as a general liaison between the caucus and executive branch agencies when helpful, particularly when members or staff need assistance obtaining information or resolving agency-related issues. • Strengthen connectivity between caucus staff and other branches of government to improve responsiveness, professional development, and institutional knowledge. • Represent the caucus on assigned committees, task forces, project teams, or external meetings as directed. • Represent members at community gatherings, stakeholder meetings, and public events when needed. 6. Other Duties • Maintain awareness of statewide issues, agency developments, caucus priorities, House Rules, legislative procedures, and political dynamics affecting members and staff. • Support caucus operations, staff planning, and legislative strategy during session and interim periods. • Perform additional tasks as assigned by the Chief of Staff, Speaker, or leadership. Job Requirements Please attach a resume with your online application or use the resume tab in DEL to provide a detailed description of how your education, training and/or experience meets each job requirement including employer, experience/responsibilities and dates (month/year) of employment/training. Bachelor's degree in Public Administration, Political Science, Business Administration, Communications, or a related field; Equivalent legislative or administrative experience may be substituted. Three to five years of progressively responsible administrative, governmental, or legislative experience. Experience working in a legislative, governmental, or public sector environment is preferred. Knowledge of parliamentary procedure is highly desirable. Additional Posting Information Work is performed primarily in a professional office environment within Legislative Hall. Extended hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, are required during legislative session and other periods of legislative activity. Position requires attendance during all scheduled House sessions and special sessions. Frequent interaction with elected officials, legislative staff, executive agencies, and members of the public. Position Characteristics: This position is one of trust and confidence within the Delaware House of Representatives. The Director of Legislative Affairs must demonstrate professionalism, impartiality, integrity, discretion, and a comprehensive understanding of legislative operations while supporting the constitutional, procedural, and administrative responsibilities of the House. The position serves as a key steward of institutional knowledge and operational continuity, helping preserve the traditions, procedures, and effective functioning of the Delaware House of Representatives across successive General Assemblies. Benefits The House of Representatives also offers paid sick and annual leave time, public employee retirement benefits, and medical, vision, and dental benefits with an employee share. Selection Process Once you have submitted your application on-line, all future correspondence related to your application will be sent via email. Please keep your contact information current.
